name: God of Prompt (@godofprompt)
overview: God of Prompt is one of the largest AI-prompt education brands on social media, run by founder Oleksandr 'Alex' Veremeyenko. It sells a library of 30,000+ ready-to-use AI prompts (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Midjourney) organized by business function, and uses Instagram, X, Threads, TikTok and Facebook as top-of-funnel for a digital-product business. It matters to @ac.wins because it is the reference model for turning 'practical AI help for non-technical business people' content into a repeatable content engine plus a low-touch digital product funnel — the same audience @ac.wins targets, but monetized via products instead of consulting.
key_metrics: Instagram: ~342K followers, 573 posts, following 18 (as of mid-2026, per Instagram profile surfaced in search). Threads: ~76.5K followers (mid-2026). X (@godofprompt): large account posting daily prompts and weekly 'AI Mastery Guides' (six-figure follower range; exact count [uncertain]). Product side: 30,000+ prompts across 19 categories; claimed 100,000+ users ('marketers, founders, and creators'); 30,000+ customers referenced in reviews; Trustpilot ~4.8/5 from ~743 reviews (as of 2026). Flagship product: Complete AI Bundle at USD 150 one-time (some listings show USD 199), lifetime updates, 7-day money-back guarantee. Instagram engagement rate: not publicly verified [uncertain].
data_recency: Follower and product data as of 2026-07 searches (profile figures 'mid-2026'). Follower counts for a fast-growing account go stale within 1-2 months; pricing and product lineup can change with promotions within weeks.
tactics_that_work: 1) Comment-to-DM lead magnets: posts ending in 'Like + comment SEND and I'll DM you the file (must be following me)' — converts reach into follows, comments (algorithm fuel) and DM-delivered lead magnets that capture emails. Documented repeatedly on their X feed (e.g., Alex Hormozi mega-prompt post, ChatGPT System Prompt post). 2) Free-value-first library: the entire 30k prompt library is browsable free on godofprompt.ai, which drives SEO traffic and reciprocity before the paid bundle upsell. 3) Borrowed authority hooks: prompts framed around famous names and books ('turn ChatGPT into Alex Hormozi', '$100M Offers') to piggyback on established demand. 4) Urgency/scarcity: 'free for 24 hours' framing on giveaways. 5) High-volume multi-platform repurposing: the same prompt content is atomized across Instagram, X, Threads, TikTok, Facebook and Medium. 6) Productized micro-offer testing: e.g., a '$1 Prompt Generator' tool as a tripwire that turns any task into a PDF guide + mega-prompt. 7) Consistent single-topic positioning: everything is prompts/agents/automation, making the account instantly legible to the algorithm and to new visitors.
content_formats: Instagram: carousel-heavy educational posts (prompt breakdowns, tip lists) plus Reels for reach — the classic aggressive carousel + Reel mix; bio drives to the prompt library. X: long text posts and threads with copy-paste mega-prompts, weekly guide threads. Threads: short conversational reposts. TikTok: short-form demo/tip videos. Blog/Medium: SEO articles ('12 Best Sora AI Prompts for Instagram Reels' etc.) that feed organic search. Direct per-format performance data for their Instagram is not public [uncertain]; industry benchmarks in 2025-26 show carousels earning ~13% more reach than Reels for engagement while Reels drive net-new discovery.
posting_cadence: Daily on X (daily prompts plus weekly 'AI Mastery Guide' threads). Instagram cadence appears to be near-daily to several posts per week (573 posts on a ~2-3 year old account) [uncertain].
hooks_and_copy_style: Hook patterns: bold claim + named authority ('Alex Hormozi's book $100M Offers has helped thousands of people print money online'), problem-agitation ('Prompt engineering is the most in-demand skill right now. But most people don't know how to write prompts.'), and giveaway CTAs. Copy is short-sentence, line-broken, benefit-first, always ending with an engagement-gated CTA: 'Like + comment [word] and I'll DM you the file (must be following me).' Tone is confident, utility-obsessed, zero fluff, lightly hype-flavored ('Steal my prompt', 'print money'). Captions function as mini sales pages for a free asset.
monetization_model: Digital products: one-time lifetime-access prompt bundles (core), category-specific prompt packs, custom GPTs/tools, a $1 tripwire generator, plus free tiers that build an email list. No services/consulting arm is visible; revenue is volume-based low-ticket digital sales fed by organic social + SEO. Affiliate/partner promotions appear occasionally [uncertain].
offer_and_pricing: Complete AI Bundle: USD 150 one-time (listed at USD 199 on some review sites), lifetime access to 30,000+ prompts across 19 categories with lifetime updates and 7-day money-back guarantee. Smaller category bundles priced below the full bundle. Free: browsable prompt library, free starter kits/lead magnets (e.g., 'ChatGPT System Prompt'). Tripwire: $1 Prompt Generator (task in, PDF guide + mega-prompt out).
audience_profile: Marketers, founders, solopreneurs and creators who want copy-paste AI results without learning prompt engineering — i.e., productivity-focused business users plus a large layer of AI-curious hobbyists. Skews global/English-speaking. This overlaps @ac.wins's SMB decision-maker ICP but is broader and shallower: buyers of a $150 bundle, not $X,000 consulting [uncertain on demographic splits].
funnel_map: Reel/carousel or X post (free prompt tease) -> CTA 'comment [keyword] + follow' -> DM automation delivers lead magnet link -> landing page captures email for free prompt pack -> email/newsletter nurture -> $1 tripwire and free library browsing -> Complete AI Bundle ($150 one-time) -> lifetime-updates lock-in and occasional new-product launches. Website SEO blog runs as a parallel entry point into the same email capture. DM-automation tooling (e.g., ManyChat) is implied by the mechanics but not publicly confirmed [uncertain].
proof_and_credibility: Social proof by volume: '100,000+ users', '30,000+ prompts', Trustpilot 4.8/5 (~743 reviews) surfaced on the site; screenshots of prompt outputs act as before/after proof inside posts; follower counts themselves (342K IG) function as authority. No client case studies — proof is aggregate usage numbers and review scores rather than named results.
takeaways_for_ac_wins: 1) Install the comment-keyword -> DM -> email funnel now: even sub-10k accounts convert well with 'comment PLAN and I'll DM you my 1-page AI checklist for [industry]' — it compounds followers, comments and an owned email list that later feeds ac-wins.com consulting calls. 2) Build one evergreen free asset with a big number ('50 plain-English AI prompts for HK small businesses') as the permanent lead magnet; God of Prompt's whole engine rests on one library asset repurposed forever. 3) Atomize: every consulting insight becomes a carousel (education/saves) + a Reel (reach) + a text post — one idea, three surfaces, matching AC's daily one-stat format. 4) Borrow authority the plain-English way: anchor posts to names/tools SMB owners already trust ('What Hormozi's offer framework looks like for a HK cafe using ChatGPT'). 5) Consider a low-ticket productized tripwire (e.g., USD 29-49 'AI Quick-Start for Non-Tech Owners' PDF/template pack) between free content and consulting — it qualifies buyers and funds ads, exactly the gap God of Prompt fills with its $1-$150 ladder.
risks_or_avoid: Do not copy the hype register ('print money', 'God of...') — it would clash with @ac.wins's plain-English, trust-first consulting brand and attract prompt-hobbyists rather than SMB decision-makers. Avoid competing on prompt-library volume; a solo consultant cannot out-catalog 30,000 prompts and the prompt-pack market is saturated and race-to-the-bottom priced. Engagement-gated giveaways done daily can train an audience to engage only for freebies. Their audience is broad and shallow; @ac.wins wins by being narrow and deep (industry-specific, HK + worldwide SMB).
platform_policy_risk: Moderate-to-high for anyone cloning this model: templated copy-paste carousels and mass-repurposed content are exactly what Meta's 2025-26 originality/aggregator deprioritization targets, and heavily AI-generated visuals may attract 'AI info' labels. Engagement-baiting CTAs ('like + comment to get X') sit close to Meta's engagement-bait guidance and could be dampened if enforcement tightens. @ac.wins should keep a human face, original examples and native commentary in every post to stay on the safe side of the originality rules.
discoverability_seo: Strong SEO posture: godofprompt.ai ranks for hundreds of 'prompts for X' queries via a large blog, and the exact-match brand name aids search. On Instagram, keyword-rich handles/captions ('AI prompts', 'ChatGPT') position them for Instagram's keyword search and Google's indexing of public IG content (live since 2025-07). Lesson for @ac.wins: put searchable phrases ('AI for small business', 'AI in plain English') in the name field, captions and alt text so posts surface in Google and IG search.
localization_language: English-only, globally targeted; no localization. This leaves the bilingual EN/Traditional-Chinese lane completely open for @ac.wins in Hong Kong — no comparable prompt-education brand serves HK SMBs in Cantonese-market Chinese.
replicability_effort: The funnel mechanics are solo-replicable: DM automation (ManyChat free-to-$15/mo), a Beehiiv/ConvertKit list (free tier), one lead-magnet PDF (a weekend to build), and 3-5 repurposed posts/week (~5-8 hrs/week with AI drafting). The non-replicable parts are the 30k-prompt catalog, multi-year daily X volume, and paid-level content throughput — a team-scale operation. Expect USD 0-50/month tool cost to copy the funnel, not the catalog.
benchmark_targets: Monthly KPIs distilled: (a) 1 comment-keyword lead-magnet post/week; target comment rate 3-5x normal posts. (b) Email capture: 100+ new emails/month from DM funnel within 90 days. (c) Follower growth: God of Prompt-style engines compound at roughly 5-10%+/month; @ac.wins target 8%/month at sub-10k. (d) Content mix: 3 carousels + 2 Reels/week minimum. (e) Trust marker: collect 10+ public testimonials/reviews (their Trustpilot 4.8/743 shows review volume as a conversion asset).
